book_title: Chapter 9. Both Sides of the Aisle, Likely Outcomes & No-FOMO Action Plan

epigraph.quote: Great companies can be mediocre trades when bought extended in a correcting tape; the edge belongs to the investor who separates business quality from entry price.
epigraph.author: Institutional Underwriting Desk

web_blocks.html: Closing Chapters 1 through 8 means holding two clear facts at once. On quality, Texas Instruments earns a solid COMPOUNDER_PASS with PASS_WITH_WATCH on KPIs. Q3 2026 sales jumped 28% YoY to $6.06B, and gross margin hit 64.2%.[2] TTM free cash flow reached $8.42B as 300mm capex stepped down toward $2B–$3B.[2][4] On price and tape, however, TXN at $303.60 trades at 26.06x forward earnings in a Correction (6 distribution days).[12][15] That yields just 1.00:1 reward-to-risk to our $345.00 base target versus our $262.00 stop. Below, we test both sides of the aisle.

Net debt climbs toward ~$12B–$13B, buybacks pause through 2028, and integration friction or wireless pricing pressure dilutes ROIC from 22.04% toward ~15%–16%.
TI.com direct channel (>80% of sales), 80,000-SKU breadth, and 40% 300mm die cost advantage defend industrial/auto share globally.
Chinese domestic rivals (SG Micro, 3PEAK, Silergy) plus Beijing's anti-dumping scrutiny erode ~19%–20% China revenue in general-purpose analog.
26.06x Fwd P/E is inline with 10Y median while EPS grows >28% next year; Stage 2 semis (rank 12) lead the next bull leg.
39.39x TTM P/E and 1.90% yield leave zero cushion in a 6-distribution-day Correction; multiple de-rates to 20x–22x on $10–$11 EPS ($225).
web_blocks.takeaway: The Bull case rests on verifiable 2026 operating leverage and capex discipline; the Bear case rests on cyclical macro/China headwinds colliding with a full 26x forward multiple.

web_blocks.html:
Three-Horizon Investment Judgment:
1. Short-Term Trading / Momentum (1–12 weeks): WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT. SPY and QQQ sit in a 6-distribution-day Correction, and TXN is 6.95% above its 50D SMA ($283.87). Chasing $303.60 yields just 1.00:1 asymmetry, so new cash waits at $278.00–$286.00 (S1 $277.54 to 30W SMA $286.10).
2. Medium-Term Inflection (3–18 months): CONSTRUCTIVE ON PULLBACKS. Q3's 64.2% gross margin and the $2B–$3B capex path already show up in free cash flow. The H1 2027 Silicon Labs close adds the next catalyst.
3. Long-Term Compounding (3–10 years): COMPOUNDER_PASS (CORE_ALPHA, TIER_2). TXN's 300mm cost edge, 80,000-SKU catalog, 22.04% ROIC, and 23-year dividend streak drive durable compounding.

Existing Position Action (Schwab Account): HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP (0 shares to sell). Our portfolio holds 1.6917 shares of TXN in schwab at a $499.98 basis (~$295.55/sh). That stake is worth $513.60 (+$13.62 / +2.72% gain, 0.58% portfolio weight, 1.64 1Y beta, 0 options).[17] TXN stays in a Stage 2 uptrend above its rising 50D ($283.87) and 200D ($264.77) averages. Since 0.58% is a modest starter weight, we hold all 1.6917 shares with a hard stop at $262.00 (under the 200D SMA and 40W EMA). We sell zero shares at $303.60.

What Invalidates the Thesis (Falsification Triggers): Institutional discipline demands clear exit rules. We would exit HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP right away if any of three events occur. First, TXN closes daily or weekly below $262.00, breaking the 200D SMA ($264.77) and 40W EMA ($264.24). Second, gross margin drops back below 60% while Days of Inventory climb past 210 days. Third, regulatory or integration delays derail the $7.5B Silicon Labs deal and its $450M synergy goal.[2][6][13]

Action Trigger: Deploy new capital—including the 2027-09-17 $280 LEAPS Call ($6,453 max loss, $344.53 breakeven)—only on a pullback into $278.00–$286.00 (2.46:1 asymmetry, consistent with WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT) or on a high-volume breakout above $334.03 once market distribution clears. Exit all 1.6917 Schwab shares immediately on any close below $262.00.

Position Sizing & Portfolio Beta Discipline: At 0.58% of total portfolio weight ($513.60 in schwab) and a 1.64 1-year beta, TXN adds modest portfolio risk.[17] If new cash enters at $278.00–$286.00, keep total sizing inside our CORE_ALPHA (TIER_2) cap. That way, a stop-out at $262.00 (-8.4% from $286.00) limits total portfolio drawdown to well under 50 bps.

web_blocks.title: Final Underwriting Verdict: COMPOUNDER_PASS | WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT ($278–$286) | HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP ($262)
paragraphs: Hold our 1.6917 Schwab shares with a hard stop at $262.00. Keep new cash sidelined until TXN tests the $278.00–$286.00 support shelf (2.46:1 asymmetry to $345.00 Base / $390.00 Bull).

book_paragraphs: To bring this underwriting dossier to an actionable conclusion, we must separate what Texas Instruments is as a business from what the stock offers at $303.60 today. Fundamentally, Texas Instruments earns an unambiguous COMPOUNDER_PASS, with a PASS_WITH_WATCH flag on operational KPIs. The company's 300mm wafer cost moat, 80,000-product catalog, direct TI.com distribution, and 22.04% return on invested capital represent the gold standard in analog semiconductors, and the 2026 financial inflection—64.2% Q3 gross margin, 28% year-over-year revenue growth, and $8.42 billion in trailing twelve-month free cash flow—confirms that the heavy lifting of the 2022–2025 buildout is paying off.

Yet great businesses are not automatically great buys at every price. Let us steelman both sides of the aisle before setting our price levels. On the bull side, if capital expenditures step down into the $2 billion to $3 billion framework in 2027 while industrial and data-center demand drives revenue past $25 billion, normalized free cash flow can expand past $10 billion to $12 billion annually. Combined with the H1 2027 close of the $7.5 billion Silicon Labs acquisition and $450 million in targeted manufacturing synergies, TXN could easily re-rate toward $390.00 per share.

On the bear side, TXN trades at 39.39 times trailing earnings and a 1.90% dividend yield while carrying 194 days of inventory. If global industrial restocking stalls, or if Chinese domestic analog competitors (SG Micro, 3PEAK, Silergy) and anti-dumping politics erode TXN's ~19%–20% China revenue, fab underutilization could linger, pushing gross margins back down toward 56%–58% and forcing a multiple contraction to 20–22 times depressed earnings—a $225.00 bear case.

Weighting these outcomes—30% probability on the $390.00 Bull case, 45% on the $345.00 Base case, and 25% on the $225.00 Bear case—yields a probability-weighted expected value of $328.50. From the current price of $303.60, that is only +8.2% expected upside, and the reward-to-risk ratio to our $345.00 base target against a $262.00 structural stop is a flat 1.00-to-1. From the $278.00 to $286.00 support shelf, however, expected value rises to +14.9% and reward-to-risk jumps to 2.46-to-1.

book_subsections.title: Three-Horizon Verdict, Schwab Position & Redeployment Plan
paragraphs: Across our three investment horizons, the playbook is crystal clear. For short-term momentum (1 to 12 weeks), our verdict is WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT: with the broader market in a 6-distribution-day Correction and TXN extended 6.95% above its 50-day moving average, new capital should sit patiently in cash for the $278.00–$286.00 buy zone. For the medium term (3 to 18 months), the setup is constructive on pullbacks as 300mm free-cash-flow expansion and the Silicon Labs integration unfold. For the long term (3 to 10 years), TXN remains a TIER_2 CORE_ALPHA compounder.

For our existing Schwab holding—1.6917 shares purchased at $499.98 ($295.55 per share), currently worth $513.60 (+2.72%, or 0.58% of portfolio weight)—the action is HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP with zero shares sold. Three explicit alerts govern the position: first, exit all 1.6917 shares on a close below $262.00 (beneath the 200-day SMA at $264.77 and 40-week EMA at $264.24); second, deploy new capital—including the 2027-09-17 $280 LEAPS Call—only in the $278.00–$286.00 support pullback zone, consistent with WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT; and third, review trailing stops and LEAPS profit-taking when TXN reaches our $345.00 base target.

Finally, our 100%-reconciled redeployment assessment leaves 100% of any sidelined capital in CASH rather than swapping into shortlist name Microsoft ($523.88, $660.00 target, 1.90:1 asymmetry) or outside peer NXP Semiconductors ($265.09, entry zone $242.42–$257.84, stop $234.07, $310.00 target, 1.65:1 asymmetry). TXN's 0.58% starter weight is appropriately sized, and its 2.46:1 asymmetry at support outranks both alternatives.

Let us double-check why we are not trimming the 1.6917 Schwab shares even though new capital is waiting for $278.00–$286.00. First, our cost basis is $295.55 per share ($499.98 total), leaving a modest +2.72% gain on a tiny 0.58% portfolio weight—well below any concentration limit. Second, TXN's 14-day RSI (54.83) and 14-week RSI (58.69) are nowhere near overbought exhaustion, and Friday's dip came on light 0.65x volume. Selling a Stage 2 compounder in a 0.58% starter slot just to try to buy it back 6% lower creates unnecessary tax friction and whipsaw risk. Instead, we let the existing starter position ride with a disciplined $262.00 hard stop while keeping 100% of new cash patient for the $278.00–$286.00 shelf.

And what would change our mind? On the upside, a high-volume weekly breakout above R1 ($318.60) and the 52-week high ($334.03) accompanied by a broad market Follow-Through Day out of Correction would allow us to ratchet our trailing stop higher. On the downside, if TXN breaks $262.00 on a closing basis—or if Q4/Q1 gross margins fall back below 60% while Days of Inventory climb back above 210 days—our thesis would shift from temporary cyclical digestion to structural overcapacity, and we would exit cleanly with zero hesitation.

This is how disciplined compounding works in practice: you do the deep fundamental work first so you know what you want to own for ten years, and then you let the tape and asymmetry math dictate the exact price at which you commit fresh capital. For Texas Instruments, the business is a COMPOUNDER_PASS, the existing 1.6917 Schwab shares stay firmly held with a $262.00 hard stop, and new capital waits patiently at $278.00–$286.00.

Take a moment to appreciate the clarity of having three binary alerts in place before the next market session opens. First, if TXN closes below $262.00, we exit all 1.6917 Schwab shares automatically—protecting capital if the Stage 2 uptrend fails. Second, if the broad market Correction pulls TXN down into the $278.00–$286.00 support shelf, we have a pre-underwritten 2.46-to-1 entry zone ready to execute without hesitation. Third, if TXN rallies to our $345.00 Base target, we ratchet the trailing stop higher and execute our LEAPS profit-taking plan. Zero guesswork, zero FOMO, and complete alignment between fundamentals and risk management.

Keep position sizing top of mind as well. Right now, our 1.6917 Schwab shares ($513.60) represent just 0.58% of portfolio weight—a low-heat CORE_ALPHA starter slot despite TXN's 1.64 one-year beta. When TXN eventually tests the $278.00–$286.00 shelf and new capital steps in, keeping total risk to a disciplined TIER_2 allocation ensures that even an unexpected stop-out at $262.00 costs less than half a percent of total portfolio value.

Let us close with a final reminder on patience. Over a ten-year holding period, whether you enter TXN at $282.00 or $303.60 might look small—yet over the first twelve months, buying at support rather than chasing into a six-distribution-day Correction is the difference between a 2.46-to-1 asymmetric setup and a 1.00-to-1 coin flip. Respect the business, respect the tape, and let the $278.00–$286.00 shelf come to you.
